name: useState()
description: A Hook that adds local state to a function component, returning the current value and a setter function to update it and trigger a re-render.
parameters: initialValue — the state's value on first render, or a function returning it (lazy initialization).
notes: setState triggers a re-render even if given the same primitive value; use the functional form `setCount(c => c + 1)` when updating based on the previous value.

name: useEffect()
description: A Hook for running side effects (data fetching, subscriptions, manually changing the DOM) after render, optionally cleaning up before the next run or on unmount.
parameters: effect — function to run after commit. deps — optional array controlling when the effect re-runs.
notes: Omitting the dependency array runs the effect after every render; an empty array `[]` runs it once on mount.

name: useContext()
description: A Hook that reads and subscribes to a Context's current value from the nearest matching Provider above the component in the tree.
parameters: MyContext — a context object created with createContext().
notes: The component re-renders whenever the Provider's value changes, even if the component only uses part of that value.

name: useRef()
description: A Hook that returns a mutable object with a `.current` property, persisting across renders without causing a re-render when it changes. Commonly used to access DOM nodes or store mutable values.
parameters: initialValue — the starting value of ref.current.
returns: A mutable ref object: { current: initialValue }.
notes: Updating ref.current does not trigger a re-render, unlike state — use it for values that shouldn't affect rendering.

name: useMemo()
syntax: const memoized = useMemo(() => computeExpensive(a, b), [a, b]);
description: A Hook that memoizes the result of an expensive calculation, only recomputing it when one of the listed dependencies changes.
parameters: factory — function that computes the value. deps — array of values the calculation depends on.
notes: Only use it for genuinely expensive computations or to preserve referential equality — overusing useMemo adds overhead without benefit.

name: useCallback()
description: A Hook that returns a memoized version of a callback function, keeping the same function reference across renders as long as its dependencies don't change.
parameters: callback — the function to memoize. deps — array of values the callback depends on.
notes: Mainly useful when passing callbacks to memoized children (React.memo) to avoid unnecessary re-renders, or as a dependency of another Hook.

name: useReducer()
description: A Hook for managing more complex state logic via a reducer function, similar to Redux, dispatching actions instead of setting state directly.
parameters: reducer — (state, action) => newState. initialState — the starting state, or an init function's result.
notes: Preferred over useState when state has multiple sub-values or the next state depends on complex logic involving the previous one.

name: useLayoutEffect()
description: Identical to useEffect, but fires synchronously after DOM mutations and before the browser paints, letting you measure or adjust layout without a visible flicker.
parameters: effect — function to run synchronously after DOM updates. deps — optional dependency array.
notes: Blocks the browser paint until it finishes, so overusing it can hurt performance — prefer useEffect unless you specifically need to avoid a visual flash.

name: Custom Hooks
syntax: function useCustomThing() { /* uses other hooks */ return value; }
description: A JavaScript function whose name starts with `use` and that calls other Hooks internally, letting you extract and reuse stateful logic across components.
returns: Whatever the custom hook chooses to return — state, functions, derived values, etc.
notes: Custom hooks share logic, not state — each component calling the hook gets its own independent state instance.

name: Rules of Hooks
description: Hooks must only be called at the top level of a function component or another Hook — never inside loops, conditions, or nested functions — so React can reliably match hook calls to state across renders.
notes: The `eslint-plugin-react-hooks` package's `rules-of-hooks` rule catches most violations automatically.

name: useId()
description: A Hook that generates a unique, stable ID string, useful for associating labels/inputs or other accessibility attributes, and safe for server-side rendering.
returns: A unique string ID stable across re-renders.
notes: Don't use useId to generate keys for list items — use data-derived keys instead.

name: useTransition()
description: A Hook that marks a state update as a non-urgent 'transition', letting React keep the UI responsive by deprioritizing that update behind more urgent ones.
returns: A [isPending, startTransition] tuple, where isPending is true while the transition is in progress.
notes: Useful for expensive re-renders (like filtering a large list) triggered by fast user input, so typing itself stays smooth.

name: useDeferredValue()
description: A Hook that returns a lagging copy of a value, letting React defer re-rendering parts of the UI that depend on it until more urgent updates finish.
returns: A deferred version of the value that updates after urgent renders complete.
notes: Similar in spirit to useTransition, but used when you don't control the state update itself (e.g. a value coming from a parent or library).

name: useImperativeHandle()
description: A Hook used with forwardRef to customize the instance value exposed to a parent's ref, exposing only specific imperative methods instead of the raw DOM node.
parameters: ref — the ref forwarded from the parent. createHandle — function returning the object to expose. deps — dependency array.
notes: Use sparingly — imperative APIs go against React's declarative model and should be reserved for cases like focus management or animations.

name: useSyncExternalStore()
description: A Hook for safely reading and subscribing to state held in a store outside React (e.g. browser APIs or third-party state libraries), avoiding tearing during concurrent rendering.
parameters: subscribe — function to register a callback for store changes. getSnapshot — returns the current value. getServerSnapshot — optional snapshot for SSR.
returns: The current snapshot value from the external store.
notes: Most state management libraries (Redux, Zustand) use this internally so their hooks work correctly with concurrent React features.
